 ( Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images ) Warriors Fall to 1-1 in NBA Cup as Spurs Win 11th Straight
 Kalyb Champion Writer & Digital Content Coordinator November 13, 2026 9:03 PM PST The Warriors fell behind 18-0 and trailed by as many as 43 points in a 123-85 NBA Cup defeat to the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center on Friday. With the loss, the Dubs fall to 1-1 in group play and have dropped consecutive games for the first time since their 0-3 start to the season. The Spurs extend the league’s longest active winning streak to 11, tying the Los Angeles Lakers for the best record in the Western Conference and move atop West Group C. Stephon Castle led the way for the Spurs with 32 points, six assists and five rebounds, while LJ Cryer paced the Warriors with a career-high 20 points and six 3-pointers.
 WARRIORS ALLOW 18 UNANSWERED POINTS TO BEGIN THE GAME 
The Warriors had their worst start in the Steve Kerr era, allowing 18 unanswered points and going scoreless for the first six minutes. The Dubs missed their first 11 shots before Gui Santos finally ended the drought, converting a layup through contact. San Antonio started 8-for-10 from the floor and built their first-half lead as large as 30 points. Golden State didn’t have a starter make more than one field goal in the first half, as LJ Cryer led the way with nine points in 10 minutes off the bench. Stephon Castle scored 18 points in the half, outscoring the Warriors’ starting five. The Spurs doubled the Warriors' shooting efficiency, shooting 50% from the floor compared to 25% for Golden State. 
 CRYER’S CAREER-HIGH 
LJ Cryer scored a career-high 20 points and sank a career-high six 3-pointers on Friday. Cryer finished as the Warriors’ leader in both categories. He has scored in double figures in three straight games, with 13 points against the Houston Rockets on Wednesday and 10 points against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday. 
 LENDEBORG ADJUSTING TO A NEW ROLE 
At pregame shootaround, rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg shared that he has to be “a lot more aggressive” with Stephen Curry out of the lineup. Lendeborg acknowledged the substantial shift in his approach and that it would take time to get comfortable in that new role. Lendeborg struggled to find a rhythm on Friday, going 1-for-13 from the field and finishing with three points in 23 minutes. 
 SPURS MOVE INTO FIRST PLACE IN WEST GROUP C 
The Warriors entered Friday’s NBA Cup matchup in first place in West Group C, with the same 1-0 record as the Spurs but holding the tiebreaker due to a slightly higher point differential. However, after losing the head-to-head matchup to San Antonio, they move behind the Spurs with two games remaining in group play. The Warriors will host the Sacramento Kings at Chase Center on Nov. 25 and visit the Portland Trail Blazers at Moda Center on Nov. 27. 
 UP NEXT  
The Warriors continue their road trip, facing the New Orleans Pelicans at Smoothie King Center on Monday (5 p.m. PT; NBCSBA).
